Article Title: Bank unions call off 3-day strike after assurances, IBA to study demands
Article Text:
Bank unions withdraw three-day strike after late-night agreement with IBA on key demands.

NEW DELHI: Bank unions called off their proposed three-day strike just before midnight after the Indian Banks Association agreed to look into their demands."A high-level committee of IBA and UFBU (United Forum of Bank Unions) will be formed immediately to deliberate on the issue of declaring the remaining Saturdays as holidays. This committee will explore, all possible alternatives; discuss with all stakeholders, and work out a solution acceptable to all stakeholders and, more importantly, the customers," a late night communication said.Unions want a five-day work week, which is being resisted by banks as it may inconvenience customers.The late-night announcement came after what turned out to be a working Sunday for state-run bank employees as govt ordered branches to stay open so that customers are not inconvenienced.
Article Summary: Unions want a five-day work week, which is being resisted by banks as it may inconvenience customers. The late-night announcement came after what turned out to be a working Sunday for state-run bank employees. Govt ordered branches to stay open so that customers are not inconvenienced.

Article Title: 'Left' in existential crisis: From CPI-CPM rift in Kerala to Delhi rout, old fault lines deepen
Article Text:
The Left faces a deeper political challenge as electoral setbacks, internal tensions and shrinking influence converge

Pinarayi probe: Another challenge after Kerala defeat

DUSU polls: Why isn't Left mobilisation becoming votes?

CPI vs CPM: When opposition itself becomes a battlefield

From Bengal to Kerala: How did the Left reach here?

What next for the Left?

There was a time when the Left’s political footprint stretched from West Bengal to Tripura and Kerala. Its influence travelled further still, through trade unions, university campuses, farmers’ movements and a cadre network that kept the red flag visible even where Communist parties were not in power. That map has steadily grown smaller.For India’s Left, the question is no longer only about shrinking electoral numbers. It is increasingly about where the Communist movement still has the political space, organisational confidence and social influence to assert itself. In Delhi, the SFI-AISA alliance has struggled to translate visible participation in student mobilisations into votes. In Kerala, the two principal constituents of the Left Democratic Front, the CPM and CPI, have found themselves publicly at odds over even the distribution of positions within the opposition, and that too after a heavy defeat in the assembly elections.These may appear to be separate battles, but they have come at a particularly difficult moment for the Left. The Kerala defeat has left it without a state government, the CPM and CPI are publicly disagreeing over the way forward, former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan is facing a probe, and the Delhi university results have again exposed the gap between the Left’s visibility in student movements and its electoral reach.The timing makes these developments particularly significant. The Left’s retreat has been a long process. The fall of the Left Front in West Bengal in 2011, the loss of Tripura in 2018 and the steady decline in its parliamentary strength had already reduced the Communist parties’ national footprint. Kerala had remained the exception, a state where the Left retained a durable organisational network and, in 2021, even broke the state’s established cycle of alternating between the LDF and UDF governments. Its defeat in 2026 means that India currently has no state government led by a Communist party.But the more revealing question may be what is happening beneath the election results. Is the Left merely going through another electoral trough, particularly after a decade in power in Kerala, or are the latest developments exposing older fault lines, from leadership and alliance tensions to the difficulty of converting traditional political mobilisation into electoral support?On September 22, the UDF government ordered a police inquiry based on an Enforcement Directorate report concerning allegations involving former chief minister and current leader of opposition Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and son-in-law PA Mohammed Riyas in the CMRL-Exalogic case. The state government said the inquiry would be entrusted to the state police; reports said it would initially be conducted by the Crime Branch without registration of an FIR.The underlying allegations are already part of an ED investigation. The agency has alleged financial irregularities involving payments made by Cochin Minerals and Rutile Ltd to Veena's now-defunct company Exalogic Solutions, and has sought action against Vijayan and others. The Kerala government's decision followed legal advice on whether the information and material supplied by the ED warranted a preliminary inquiry.For the CPM, however, the political dimension is inseparable from the legal one. Party general secretary MA Baby has said the party will fight the matter “legally and politically”, while accusing central agencies of having been used against opposition leaders.That places the Left in an unfamiliar position in Kerala. For a decade, Vijayan and the CPM were operating from government. Now the former chief minister is leading the opposition while facing a probe ordered by the government that replaced him.The probe comes only months after the LDF lost power following a decade in government, at a time when the CPM is already examining what went wrong and trying to regroup in opposition. The question is therefore not simply whether the allegations withstand investigation. The episode also puts Vijayan and the record of the previous government back under scrutiny at a particularly difficult moment for the party.The Delhi University Students' Union election offers a different window into the Left's problem, particularly its ability to convert activism and issue-based mobilisation into electoral support.The SFI-AISA alliance had been visible in campaigns around issues including student housing, examinations and accountability, and had participated prominently in the CJP mobilisation. Yet its electoral numbers declined in three of the four central-panel contests compared with 2025. Its presidential candidate Ananya Raturi received 5,377 votes, almost identical to the 5,385 polled by the alliance's candidate last year. But its vice-presidential tally fell from 4,163 to 2,383, the secretary vote from 9,535 to 8,734 and the joint-secretary vote from 8,425 to 5,837.The results also showed that student politics cannot simply be read as a binary contest between the major national parties and the Left. ABVP won three of the four central-panel positions, while Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen won the vice-president's post with 30,615 votes. He had previously been associated with Congress-affiliated NSUI but contested independently after not receiving its ticket.For the Left, the striking element is the gap between mobilisation and electoral conversion. A political organisation can be prominent in protests, articulate grievances on campuses and participate in wider movements, but that visibility does not automatically translate into votes.The presidential contest is particularly revealing. The Left candidate finished with 5,377 votes, while ABVP's Yash Dabas won with 24,576 and NSUI's Vijay Shankar Meena polled 22,523. The result does not erase the Left's presence on campus, but it does expose the difficulty of turning that presence into control of student institutions.And that is why the DUSU result matters beyond one university election. Student politics has historically been an important space for the Left to recruit, organise and build its next generation of political workers. Sitaram Yechury, for instance, rose through student politics at JNU before eventually becoming CPI(M) general secretary.The question for the Left now is simpler: if it can still bring young people to protests and movements, why is it struggling to bring them to the ballot box?The strain is also visible inside Kerala's Left alliance. After the LDF's assembly defeat, the CPI demanded the post of deputy leader of the opposition in the assembly, arguing for a larger role within the alliance. The CPM, however, rejected the demand, with Vijayan publicly opposing it.On the surface, the disagreement is about a post. But underneath it is a larger debate about how the LDF should function after its election defeat. The CPI has argued for greater sharing of responsibilities and “collective leadership”, while the CPM has maintained that the alliance should follow its established conventions.The disagreement soon spilled into public. CPI state secretary Binoy Viswam criticised Vijayan's stand, while senior CPI leader C Divakaran went further and questioned Vijayan's authority to dismiss the demand. Divakaran also argued that Vijayan should have taken responsibility for the election defeat rather than becoming leader of the opposition.The CPM pushed back too. CPM state secretariat member C N Mohanan questioned the CPI's electoral strength and accused it of using pressure tactics against the larger ally.The dispute may appear procedural because the deputy leader's post is largely an organisational and parliamentary position. But its political significance lies elsewhere. The CPI has sought greater recognition after the LDF's defeat, while the CPM, as the dominant force in the alliance, remains the principal party responsible for its direction.The two parties have since tried to prevent the dispute from escalating further. But the episode illustrates a problem that often becomes sharper after an electoral defeat: who takes responsibility for the loss, and who gets to decide the course correction?Kerala's 2026 verdict completed a long retreat. West Bengal's Left Front had ruled continuously from 1977 until 2011, while Tripura remained under Left Front rule for 25 years before the BJP ended that run in 2018. Kerala subsequently became the Left's last major governing base.But the story of the Left's decline has not been the same everywhere. In West Bengal, the 2011 defeat ended 34 years of uninterrupted Left Front rule and the Communist parties have since struggled to recover their old electoral space. In Tripura, the BJP displaced the Left after 25 years in power and emerged as its principal rival. Kerala followed a different trajectory, with power traditionally alternating between the LDF and Congress-led UDF.That is what made the LDF's 2021 victory particularly significant. The Vijayan government returned for a second consecutive term, breaking Kerala's four-decade pattern of alternating governments and giving the Left something it no longer had elsewhere: a state where it could demonstrate that it remained capable not only of surviving, but of retaining power.The 2026 defeat is therefore different from Bengal and Tripura and cannot automatically be equated with the organisational collapse witnessed elsewhere. Yet the scale of the setback raises questions beyond normal anti-incumbency. The LDF was reduced from 94 seats to 35, while the UDF won 102. The CPI(M) also suffered defeats in areas traditionally associated with its organisation, including parts of Kannur. BJP candidates won three seats, Chathannoor, Nemom and Kazhakoottam, including constituencies that had been held by LDF leaders.The larger national trajectory has been just as stark. At its parliamentary peak in 2004, the Left parties together had 59 Lok Sabha MPs and provided crucial outside support to the first UPA government. Twenty-two years later, their presence in Parliament and across state governments is a fraction of what it was.The decline cannot be traced to a single election or a single cause. The Left has had to contend with the loss of old strongholds, changes in the nature of work and organised labour, the rise of powerful regional parties, the BJP's expansion into states where the Left once had substantial space, and the challenge of reaching a generation of voters with little memory of the Communist parties at the height of their political influence.Kerala had, for years, stood apart from that national decline. The 2026 result does not mean the Left's organisational base in the state has disappeared, but it has removed its last seat of state power and made the problems elsewhere much harder to ignore.With no Communist-led state government left, a diminished parliamentary presence, weaker conversion of student mobilisation into votes and visible friction among its own principal parties, the Left finds itself at one of its most difficult political moments.The challenge is no longer simply how to win the next election. It is whether the political space that once made the Communist movement a national force can still be reconstructed, and whether the Left can address its old fault lines while finding its place in a changing political landscape.
Article Summary: The Left faces a deeper political challenge as electoral setbacks, internal tensions and shrinking influence converge. The Kerala defeat has left it without a state government, the CPM and CPI are publicly disagreeing over the way forward. Former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan is facing a probe, and the Delhi university results have again exposed the gap between the Left’s visibility in student movements and its electoral reach.

Article Title: PM Modi pens tribute to Ashok Singhal: 'A great personality who was committed to nation-building'
Article Text:

There is a beautiful saying that the tree does not consume its own fruit, nor does the river retain its waters. Both exist for the benefit of others. Our saints and seers have long taught us that a life devoted to the welfare of those around us acquires a meaning far greater than individual achievement. If there is one person in whom this spirit was constantly reflected, it was Shri Ashok Singhal ji.Starting Sept 27, we mark his birth centenary to celebrate an outstanding personality who brought together spiritual pursuit, cultural awakening and decades of dedicated organisational work.I consider it a privilege that I had innumerable opportunities to interact with Ashok ji and receive his affection. One of the earliest instances dates back to 1981, when I was a young karyakarta going about the organisational duties given to me. I received a handwritten letter from him. Naturally, it was a noteworthy moment for me. He talked about an important upcoming programme and gave a few tasks to be done.Over several decades, I saw him work day and night. He would undertake long and often difficult travels to the remotest of areas. He was particularly passionate about travelling across tribal areas of Gujarat. His mind was constantly running, thinking about what more one can do for those on the margins of society.Whenever any part of the nation was affected by a natural disaster, Ashok ji was either among the first to reach there himself or among those guiding karyakartas to help those affected. My own experience with him in the aftermath of the 2001 Kutch earthquake was unforgettable.This spirit of compassion and care for others is something that came to Ashok ji very early in his life. He hailed from a very illustrious and prosperous family. His father, Shri Mahavir ji, was a distinguished administrator. One of his bro-thers, Shri BP Singhal ji, went on to become a police officer and later a member of Parliament. Another brother, Shri VP Singhal ji, was the chief secretary of Tripura when the state was just formed. Other family members succeeded in the world of commerce and agriculture. But from a young age, Ashok ji was attracted to something else altogether... the revival of Bharat and bringing glory to Maa Bharti's children.Growing up in Prayagraj, Ashok ji would sit for hours on the banks of the Sangam. The river naturally interested him, but so did the people who came, such as saints, seers and devotees. It nurtured an understanding of India's cultural ethos and strengthened his intention to do something for society. This desire to live for others drew him to RSS. He embraced every responsibility that came his way with enthusiasm, discipline and a sense of duty.Ashok ji nurtured institutions and movements through persistence and hard work. He was blessed with a formidable voice and an oratory that could hold an entire gathering in its spell. Equally noteworthy was his care for fellow karyakartas. Anyone who came into contact with him could not help but marvel at his remarkable simplicity. He shared a deep bond with Sant Samaj and commanded immense respect among saints and seers across the country. They valued his counsel and listened to him with great regard.My mind goes back to two instances which brought out the legendary persona of Shri Ashok Singhal ji. The first was in 1993, when Vishwa Hindu Parishad organised a convention in US to mark 100 years since Swami Vivekananda's Chicago address. The vision to host such a conference overseas, the planning and the bringing together of diverse stakeholders revealed the organisational genius of Ashok ji.The second instance is from 2000. World Hindu Conference was organised in Port of Spain in Trinidad and Tobago. I could see how his presence ignited so much enthusiasm among other delegates. After my address, his words of appreciation were a very moving experience for me. I saw yet again how his encouragement filled every karyakarta with so much energy.No mention of Shri Ashok Singhal ji is complete without recalling his pivotal role in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Who can forget his address at Boat Club Rally in 1991? Or the defining image of an injured and bleeding Ashok ji at the peak of the movement. Today, if there is a grand Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, it is because of stalwarts like him who selflessly immersed themselves in the effort to make it possible. He would have been the happiest person on seeing Ram Mandir take shape in Ayodhya.Shri Ashok Singhal ji was blessed with remarkable clarity of thought and one area wh-ere it was clearly seen was his belief that our society needs to be harmonious, that the message of brotherhood has to be reaffirmed. He worked towards strengthening social unity and equality. He firmly believed that there could be no distinction of any kind in society and that every individual deserved equal dignity and respect. It was his thought that the first brick of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya would be laid by Shri Kameshwar Choupal Ji, a grassroots VHP karyakarta from Bihar who hailed from the marginalised sections of society. At a dharm sansad in Kashi, he decided that the Dom Raja would be honoured and went on to work with him as part of various community efforts.Beyond nation-building, Ashok ji had two areas that were very close to his heart: education (especially Vedic education) and music. As the MP from Varanasi, I feel very proud that the city I represent, the eternal Kashi, has played its part in Ashok ji's life. He was educated at BHU and was also known to be a good student. He was closely associated with the Ekal Vidyalaya initiative, which worked to extend basic education to remote villages, especially among tribal communities.He was a voracious reader as well as a good listener, and he always told younger karyakartas to read as much as possible.Those who knew Ashok ji closely knew how well he sang. I recall meetings in Nagpur, where he would sing the Ekal Geet, leaving everyone mesmerised and setting the tone for the meeting. A video of him surprising everyone and singing 'Yeh Matru Bhumi Meri, Yeh Pitra Bhumi Meri' during his 90th birthday celebrations in 2015 went viral.On his birth centenary, let us ensure that more youngsters know about his greatness. And let us renew our pledge to realise his dreams for our nation and our people.
Article Summary: Shri Ashok Singhal ji's birth centenary is on September 27. He was an outstanding personality who brought together spiritual pursuit, cultural awakening and decades of dedicated organisational work. Anyone who came into contact with him could not help but marvel at his remarkable simplicity.

Article Title: SIR tweaks proof of ‘disaster’, says Congress; Akhilesh to skip INDIA bloc meet
Article Text:
SIR row escalates: Jairam Ramesh calls EC press note ‘desperate damage control’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress Sunday continued with its protest against EC, saying the proposed measures related to special intensive revision of electoral rolls were an admission that the exercise had been a "disaster". It added the "piecemeal measures" for deleted or at-risk voters would do little to mitigate "mass disenfranchisement".Congress's statement came amid mobilisation by the opposition to coordinate with INDIA bloc members and non-NDA parties as they prepare to further their protest. While top members of the alliance are expected to attend the INDIA bloc meeting on Sept 30, Congress sources said SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had told the party brass that Rajya Sabha nominations for 10 seats in UP were starting and so he would send senior party members.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said the party would hold district-level protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Monday.Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh said the press note issued by EC had been debunked and exposed for what it was - "a desperate attempt at damage control that hides all and reveals nothing". What was the point of this SIR process that had turned into a "colossal waste" of public resources and nuisance for every citizen, he asked.In another development, CPM general secretary M A Baby met AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal Sunday. "Kejriwal said there has to be a very powerful struggle exposing the manner in which EC has been working as a tool in the hands of the union," Baby said.
Article Summary: Congress says proposed measures related to special intensive revision of electoral rolls were an admission that the exercise had been a "disaster" It added the "piecemeal measures" for deleted or at-risk voters would do little to mitigate "mass disenfranchisement" CPM general secretary M A Baby met AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal Sunday.

Article Title: HM Amit Shah recalls Ashok Singhal's role in Ram temple movement
Article Text:
Home minister Amit Shah on Sunday hailed former VHP leader Ashok Singhal as an inspiration, saying his life and dedication remained worthy of emulation.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Lauding former VHP leader Ashok Singhal as an inspiration and hero, home minister Amit Shah Sunday said Singhal believed that India could attain a position of glory only by removing the "stigma of slavery" and constructing a grand Ram temple in its place in Ayodhya "The essence of his life, his penance, his simplicity and his dedication and endeavour are qualities worthy of emulation by every young person," Shah said at the inaugural ceremony of the centenary year celebrations to mark his birth anniversary. RSS general secretary Dattatreya Hosabole was among the Hindutva figures present at the event.It was only after PM Narendra Modi took office that govt obstacles were removed and a grand Ram temple was built, Shah said. He said the image of Singhal wiping blood from his face during a police lathicharge ordered by the then UP govt against Ram temple activists should remain etched in the memory of the youth for 100 years."Ashok ji believed that one should remain committed to Hindutva because the welfare of the entire universe is possible only on the basis of the ideals of Hindutva," Shah said.Born into a well-off family, Singhal joined RSS and later became the fiery face of the temple movement as a VHP leader. He is credited with expanding the defining Hindutva movement by bringing deprived sections of society, especially sections of Dalits and tribals, under its fold.When a nation and society do not remember their heroes and fail to take their lives and teachings to the youth, an ideological vacuum emerges, Shah said, calling for promotion of Singhal's life story.
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah on Sunday hailed former VHP leader Ashok Singhal as an inspiration. He said Singhal believed that India could attain a position of glory only by removing the "stigma of slavery" and constructing a grand Ram temple in its place in Ayodhya.

Article Title: F-35 fighter jets, 200+ airmen arrive as US participates in India's Tarang Shakti air exercise
Article Text:
Gor said he looked forward to see American firth-generation fighters planes flying alongside the Indian jets (Photo: AP).

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Six American F-35 fighter jets, along with more than 200 US airmen touched down in Jodhpur on Saturday to take part in the second edition of multinational air exercise, Tarang Shakti.US Ambassador Sergio Gor announced their arrival in his post on X, informing first ever American participation in the exercise.Gor said he looked forward to see American firth-generation fighters planes flying alongside the Indian jets.The second edition of Tarang Shakti got underway at Air Force Station Jodhpur in Rajasthan on Saturday, with more than 40 countries taking part in the drills.In a post on X, the Indian Air Force extended a welcome to the participating contingents, saying, "A warm welcome to our friends from across the skies as they touch down at Jodhpur. Welcome to India. Welcome to Tarang Shakti."Announcing the 2026 edition, the Indian Air Force said, "Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 returns as India's premier multinational air exercise, bringing global Air Forces together for high-octane joint tactical manoeuvres. Stay tuned as elite aviators take to the skies!"Earlier, Gor and lieutenant general Vikrant Suresh Deshpande, general officer commanding, 10 Corps, observed a joint firing demonstration by Indian and US Army personnel at the Mahajan Field Firing Range as part of Exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026, showcasing the depth and complexity of bilateral training between the two forces.The demonstration showcased the Pinaka multi-barrel rocket launcher, M777 ultra-light howitzer and Dhanush artillery system, alongside AH-64E Apache attack helicopters, L70 air-defence guns and Swathi weapon-locating radars.For its part, the US Army deployed HIMARS and M-LIDS systems, bringing together a wide range of artillery, aviation, air-defence and surveillance capabilities in a challenging field setting.The first edition of Tarang Shakti was held in 2024, with defence minister Rajnath Singh describing it at the time as a step towards deepening cooperation, coordination and trust among partner nations.
Article Summary: The second edition of Tarang Shakti got underway at Air Force Station Jodhpur in Rajasthan on Saturday. US Ambassador Sergio Gor announced their arrival in his post on X, informing first ever American participation in the exercise. Gor said he looked forward to see American firth-generation fighters planes flying alongside the Indian jets.

Article Title: After arriving in the US with $500, former tennis player Andres Bernal began investing in Connecticut real estate in 2016; a decade later, he says he owns more than 60 rental units worth over $12 mill
Article Text:
Bernal's approach has also evolved with the performance of individual properties. He and his partners have sold some older Connecticut properties where substantial equity was tied up but cash flow no longer justified holding them.

From tennis courts to property seals

A portfolio built around different tenants

Building the business behind the properties

Knowing when to hold and when to sell

When Andres Bernal arrived in the United States with $500, his immediate goal was not to build a real estate empire. The Dominican-born former professional tennis player had come to pursue the sport he had played since childhood. But after years of teaching tennis and working long hours, he began looking for a different route to financial independence.Real estate, a concept he had first encountered through his family in the Dominican Republic, eventually became that route. His first investment came in 2016. Nearly a decade later, Bernal says his Connecticut portfolio has grown to more than 60 rental units valued at over $12 million, states a podcast interview published by Harbordise Partners.Bernal's introduction to real estate began long before his first investment. His godfather was a builder in the Dominican Republic, and Bernal had watched him acquire and develop property while growing up.After playing professional tennis for nearly two years in the US, Bernal began teaching the sport, sometimes working 50 to 60 hours a week. Looking for a way to build income beyond trading time for money, he started studying stocks, businesses and real estate, states the interview.He eventually focused on property investing, learning the fundamentals before making his first investment in 2016.The strategy has since expanded beyond long-term rentals. Bernal completed more than 50 property flips during 2024 and 2025, building a business around acquisitions, renovations and sales while continuing to grow his rental portfolio.According to the video interview, his Connecticut holdings include multifamily properties, duplexes, single-family homes and student rentals. Some properties operate through the federal Section 8 housing program, while others serve traditional tenants. Student housing has become an important part of the portfolio. Bernal owns properties near three Connecticut universities and typically rents homes to groups of students whose parents or family members co-sign their leases. Keeping properties within walking distance of campuses is another central part of the strategy, reducing the need for parking and transportation.His Section 8 properties provide another source of rental income, although they come with additional inspections and administrative requirements. Bernal says he has about 22 units connected to the program.Managing dozens of properties and completing frequent flips requires more than finding deals. Bernal has built a network of contractors and property-management support to keep the operation moving. His flipping operation includes about a dozen contractors handling work such as carpentry, painting and basic plumbing and electrical tasks. A smaller part-time team manages the rental portfolio. That structure allows the same network of workers to move between renovation projects and maintenance needs, reducing the need to constantly find new contractors.Bernal's approach has also evolved with the performance of individual properties. He and his partners have sold some older Connecticut properties where substantial equity was tied up but cash flow no longer justified holding them. His renovation philosophy follows a similar hierarchy. Safety, structural problems and major mechanical issues come first, followed by improvements that can increase rental value and appeal. Cosmetic upgrades come later when the numbers support them.For Bernal, the bigger lesson from a decade in real estate has been discipline. Deals need to be conservatively underwritten, renovation budgets need room for surprises, and projected resale values cannot be treated as guarantees.What began with $500 and a career on the tennis court has evolved into a Connecticut real estate business spanning rentals, student housing, affordable housing and property flips.Images Courtesy: Facebook and istock
Article Summary: Andres Bernal arrived in the United States with $500 and a career on the tennis court. The Dominican-born former professional tennis player had come to pursue the sport he had played since childhood. After years of teaching tennis and working long hours, he began looking for a different route to financial independence. His first investment came in 2016 and his Connecticut portfolio has grown to more than 60 rental units valued at over $12 million.

Article Title: “An F”: Caitlin Clark accepts failure as Indiana Fever crushed by Aces in A'ja Wilson's 38-point showdown
Article Text:
Caitlin Clark reacts to Fever's loss against Aces. Image via: Getty Images

Why Caitlin Clark gave the Fever defense an F in Game 1

Raven Johnson gives Caitlin Clark and the Fever one bright spot

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Caitlin Clark kept her postgame review short. Asked to grade the Indiana Fever defense, she said, "An F." Few could argue.The Las Vegas Aces took the first-round opener 102-85 on Sunday, and A'ja Wilson did most of the damage with 38 points and 16 rebounds. Indiana now has one game left to keep its season alive, and the defense needs a lot of work before then.Caitlin Clark's grade came after the Fever allowed 102 points on Sunday, and the numbers back it up. Las Vegas shot 59 percent overall and 47 percent from three. It was one of those nights when nearly every possession ended in a clean look.Wilson was the center of it all. The reigning WNBA MVP hit 15 of 19 shots and tied a playoff career high with 38 points. She also pulled down 16 rebounds, blocked four shots, stole the ball twice, handed out two assists and knocked down two threes. Indiana had no real answer for her.The Fever guard had a rough night at the other end too. Clark scored 15 points on 6-of-17 shooting, though she did add 10 assists for a double-double. Kelsey Mitchell struggled even more, hitting 4 of 16 for 12 points. Aliyah Boston led Indiana with 18, and Sophie Cunningham chipped in 13 off the bench.It was not enough to keep pace with an Aces offense that barely missed.Indiana lost backup guard Tyasha Harris to a season-ending leg injury in the last regular-season game. Coach Stephanie White had said before the playoffs that rookie Raven Johnson could help fill the gap. She did.Johnson played 22 minutes off the bench in the postseason debut and scored 14 points on 6-of-7 shooting. She added two steals, an assist and a three-pointer. The two-time NCAA champion at South Carolina looked comfortable on a night when few teammates did. White said Johnson "did great" and gave the team the lift it needed on both ends.Clark, the newly crowned AP Comeback Player of the Year, was just as impressed with the 5-foot-8 rookie. She liked the offense, but she singled out the defensive intensity as exactly what Indiana needs from here on. In her view, Johnson puts in the work and can be counted on.Now the margin is gone. Game 2 is Tuesday at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, with tipoff set for 6:30 p.m. ET. A second loss ends the Fever's season. Clark and her teammates will need far more resistance against Wilson and an Aces attack that hit almost everything in Game 1.
Article Summary: Caitlin Clark gave the Indiana Fever defense an F in Game 1. A'ja Wilson did most of the damage with 38 points and 16 rebounds. Game 2 is Tuesday at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, with tipoff set for 6:30 p.m. ET.

Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, is busy gearing up for the new season after signing a $116 million extension with the team. While Stephen Curry is a multi millionaire and is a popular athlete, his wife, Ayesha Curry , has carved out her new career. Weeks ahead of the new season, Ayesha Curry has opened up about managing her businesses.In an interview with Pure Wow, Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry reflects on managing motherhood and her work as she said, “I often tell people that you don’t know how much you can get done in a day until you have kids. Not only has being a parent made me push myself in terms of productivity, but also in that I’m now accountable to more than myself.”Stephen Curry’s wife, the popular entrepreneur, actress and chef, Ayesha Curry added, “I am working hard to build something for my kids and to be someone who they can be proud of, which influences every decision I make professionally.”Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry also reflected on how she has been able to work from home to help reduce her work load as she added, “While I’m required to travel often for work, which forces me to be away from the kids, I am fortunate to have the ability to primarily run my team and website out of my home.”She continued, “So I’m still able to be with my son throughout the day and can be there to hug the girls when they get home from school and do all the other mommy duties I love.There can be some chaotic moments, and occasionally there will be a 7-year-old quietly coloring in the corner of a staff meeting, but it works for us.”While the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry has been a popular athlete for close to two decades now, his wife Ayesha Curry also had a passion for starting something of her own.After a pretty successful career in movies and being a chef, Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry launched her popular skincare brand, Sweet July, in 2023 and has been pretty busy with it ever since.While Ayesha Curry was pretty nervous before starting her own venture, Sweet July has been highly successful as it remains inspired by her Jamaican heritage.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have also extended the concept to cafes in Charlotte as the skincare brand has now become a household name across the nation.

Article Title: At 19, Pincky Balhara lost three family members ahead of Asian Games debut; Now, she is only Indian to win multiple Kurash medals
Article Text:
Bronze medalists Pincky Balhara of India (AP Photo)

What is Kurash?

From judo mats to Kurash

Three deaths changed everything

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pincky Balhara's Asian Games record

Year Games Category Result 2018 Jakarta Women's -52kg 🥈 Silver 2022 Hangzhou Women's Kurash Quarterfinal 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Women's -78kg 🥉 Bronze

Three family deaths in quick succession could have brought Pincky Balhara’s sporting journey to a halt. Instead, the Delhi athlete carried her grief into the competition arena, turned her father’s dream into motivation and went on to win an Asian Games medal.Eight years after her historic silver at the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games, Balhara returned to the continental podium on Monday, winning bronze in the women’s -78kg Kurash event at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Games. The bronze is Balhara’s second Asian Games medal in Kurash, following her silver in the women’s -52kg category in Jakarta. She has now become the only Indian athlete to win multiple Asian Games medals in Kurash.Kurash is a traditional Central Asian martial art that originated in the region and is particularly associated with Uzbekistan. It made its Asian Games debut at the 2018 Jakarta Games. The basic objective is simple: throw the opponent onto their back while remaining in a standing position. Unlike judo or Brazilian jiu-jitsu, Kurash does not involve prolonged ground fighting.Born on October 20, 1998, in Neb Sarai, Delhi, Balhara began training in judo when she was nine. Her maternal uncle, Samundar Tokas, a former judoka and coach, played a major role in her early development.She quickly established herself in judo, winning gold at the 2018 Asian Junior Judo Championships. But she missed out on India's judo squad for the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games. That disappointment opened another door.With Kurash making its Asian Games debut in Jakarta, Balhara entered the trials. The sport, which shares similarities with judo but is contested entirely from a standing position, offered her another route to the continental stage. She made the team and was soon heading to Jakarta.But just weeks before the Games, Balhara's life was shattered. She lost her cousin brother first, followed by her father, who died of a heart attack, and then her grandfather. The three deaths came in quick succession, leaving the teenager struggling to cope with the loss.Her father had been particularly excited about her selection for the Asian Games. After his death, Balhara initially did not want to compete. Her uncle, however, pushed her to continue, reminding her of her father's hopes for her career.She returned to training while dealing with grief and also had to make the weight for her 52kg category. She later recalled going to the gym at night because she feared people would judge her for returning to training so soon after her father's death.Balhara eventually made it to the 2018 Asian Games and produced a remarkable run. At just 19, she reached the women's -52kg Kurash final, becoming one of India's first Asian Games medallists in the sport. She eventually lost to Uzbekistan's Gulnor Sulaymanova and settled for silver.Balhara later recalled her father's prediction before the Games: that she would win silver rather than gold. When she finished second, she remembered his words. At Aichi-Nagoya, Balhara began her campaign with a 3-0 quarterfinal victory over South Korea's Garam Lim, securing her place in the semifinals and guaranteeing India another Kurash medal.She then faced South Korea's Sumin Mo in the last four. Mo won 5-0, sending Balhara into the bronze-medal position.Eight years after her first Asian Games medal, Balhara was back on the podium.
Article Summary: Pincky Balhara won bronze in the women’s -78kg Kurash event at the 2026 Aichi- Nagoya Games. It is her second Asian Games medal in Kurash, following her silver at the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games. She has now become the only Indian athlete to win multiple Asian Games medals in the martial art.

Article Title: 'Chilli powder in eyes': Fashion design graduate, sister ram scooter into Delhi delivery boy, rob him
Article Text:
A fashion design graduate and her Class 12 dropout sister were arrested for robbing a delivery boy in Rohini. (Photo credit: X)





NEW DELHI: A fashion design graduate and her Class 12 dropout sister were arrested for allegedly robbing a delivery boy in Rohini , police said.One of them posed as a customer and tried to snatch parcels from his delivery bag, while the other allegedly arrived on a scooty and struck him from behind.DCP (Rohini) Shashank Jaiswal said the incident took place around 7.20pm on Sept 25 near Hanuman mandir in Sector 5. One of the women allegedly approached the delivery boy posing as a customer and attempted to forcibly take parcels from his bag.When he resisted, she allegedly threw chilli powder into his eyes. Meanwhile, the second woman arrived on a scooty and allegedly struck him from behind, causing him to fall and sustain a leg injury. The two then fled with several parcels.“This is so far their first target. We are looking into whether they may have been involved in similar incidents earlier,” Jaiswal said.A case under sections 309(6) (voluntarily causing hurt while committing robbery) and 3(5) (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of BNS was registered at Budh Vihar police station.Following the incident, a team was formed to investigate the case.Police said technical surveillance and human intelligence helped identify the accused as Nancy Singh, 26, and Gracy Singh , 20, both residents of Karol Bagh. Police arrested the sisters within 15 hours of registering the case.Three robbed parcels, along with the mobile phone and scooty allegedly used in the offence, were recovered from their possession, police said. During interrogation, the accused allegedly disclosed their involvement in the case.Police said Nancy had completed a fashion design course but was unemployed, while Gracy was a Class 12 dropout. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A fashion design graduate and her Class 12 dropout sister were arrested for allegedly robbing a delivery boy in Rohini. One of them posed as a customer and tried to snatch parcels from his delivery bag. The other allegedly arrived on a scooty and struck him from behind.

Article Title: Trapped hand, speeding SUV and desperate climb: How cops stopped gutka-laden vehicle
Article Text:
Head constable, M Velmurugan, claimed that the chase started at Vilankurichi and he clung on to the SUV till Karumathampatti, which is about 40km away.

,





COIMBATORE: A police head constable foiled an attempt by three smugglers to escape in a gutka-laden sports utility vehicle, by clinging to the top of the vehicle on Avinashi Road till a highway patrol team intercepted the gang at Karumathampatti near here on Sunday morning.Head constable, M Velmurugan, claimed that the chase started at Vilankurichi and he clung on to the SUV till Karumathampatti, which is about 40km away. The three smugglers have been arrested.Acting on a tip-off, a police team led by Kovilpalayam sub-inspector Vignesh and head constable Velmurugan attempted to stop the SUV (KA 05 NG 7692) at Vilankurchi near Kovilapalayam around 5.45am.Velmurugan climbed atop the SUV when the driver slowed the vehicle but refused to halt and sped towards Avinashi. The constable clung atop the SUV by holding the roof rails of the vehicle despite the smugglers driving the vehicle athigh speed.Vignesh immediately informed the Karumathampatti police and highway patrol team on Avinashi Road, who chased the vehicle for nearly an hour and eventually intercepted it at Karumathampatti and saved Velmurugan without any injuries.Police found more than 100kg of gutka products in the car and identified three smugglers travelling in the car as P Babu Dhara, 27, A Rajesh, 23 and S Suresh, 20, all from Rajasthan.They were smuggling the contraband from Karnataka to Coimbatore. Police seized the contraband and the car.Meanwhile, prohibition and excise minister K Vignesh and minister for backward classes welfare RS Rajakannappan spoke to Velmurugan over a video call and congratulated him for his bravery.They said they would take Velmurugan’s daring act to the attention of chief minister C Joseph Vijay.Later, Velmurugan told TOI“When we approached the vehicle, the driver stopped and rolled down the window. While we were questioning the occupants, he started moving the car and closed the window, trapping the SI’s hand inside. Our SI ran for a few metres with his hand trapped inside. Luckily, the SI fell on the road without any injuries, but I climbed atop the SUV. I realised the suspects should not be allowed to escape, so I held on to the rails tightly till they were captured. As police personnel, we were just doing our duty.”
Article Summary: Head constable, M Velmurugan, claimed that the chase started at Vilankurichi and he clung on to the SUV till Karumathampatti, which is about 40km away. The three smugglers have been arrested. Police seized the contraband and the car.

Article Title: 2 killed as speeding Range Rover hits stray bull, rams divider on Bharatmala Highway in Gujarat
Article Text:
Two young men lost their lives in a tragic accident on the Bharatmala Highway.





PALANPUR: Two young men were killed and another seriously injured after their Range Rover travelling from Rajkot towards Rajasthan, met with a fatal accident on the Bharatmala Highway near Tharad early on September 27.The accident took place near Malpur on the Tharad-Deesa Highway when a stray bull suddenly came onto the road. The Range Rover struck the animal and then rammed into the highway divider. The collision was so intense that debris from the vehicle and body remains were strewn across the road.The SUV was registered in Rajkot.Locals who reached the spot alerted the 108 emergency ambulance service. Two of the three occupants died at the spot, while the injured man was initially taken for treatment and later shifted to Ahmedabad.One of the deceased was from Amreli and the other from Rajkot. Their bodies were taken to Tharad Civil Hospital for post-mortem.
Article Summary: Accident took place near Malpur on the Tharad-Deesa Highway. The Range Rover struck the animal and then rammed into the highway divider. Two of the three occupants died at the spot, while the injured man was initially taken for treatment and later shifted to Ahmedabad.

NEW DELHI: Hardik Pandya 's return to competitive cricket has been delayed again as the all-rounder is set to miss the three India A fixtures against Australia A in Puducherry starting October 6. The all-rounder experienced pain in his right shin again earlier this week and underwent a fresh set of scans. The BCCI medical team monitoring him has advised further rest.The 32-year-old was inching closer to a return to cricket but the recurring shin issue has derailed all the progress he made at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in the last few months.It was the same issue that ruled him out of selection for the Afghanistan T20Is. It is understood that he was also being considered for a late entry into the Asian Games but the unfortunate turn of events occurred close to selection day - first before the Afghanistan ODIs and then later for the T20Is against the same opposition.With no physical activity for the next 10-15 days, it remains highly doubtful that Pandya will be available for the T20Is against New Zealand next month as well. The selectors would also operate with caution when considering him directly for the ODIs which follow the five T20Is. The team management's frustrating wait for their premier all-rounder continues, but they understand that a rushed approach will not be followed as the 2027 World Cup remains the ultimate goal.There is no official word from the Indian cricket board yet. However, Suryansh Shedge is currently taining at the BCCI CoE and could well be drafted as Hardik 's replacement for three India A games.

Article Title: Chess Olympiad Round 9: D Gukesh channels his world champion self, overturns almost-lost game to keep India in gold hunt
Article Text:
Dommaraju Gukesh of India (Photo by Rafal Oleksiewicz for FIDE)

How Gukesh turned the tables on Donchenko

Vantika, Divya lead India's women to victory

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

ALSO READ:

NEW DELHI: Since becoming world champion two years ago, noise has followed Dommaraju Gukesh almost everywhere, at times making it feel as though he isn't worthy of the title he rightfully won.But on Friday, when India needed the youngest world champion in history to deliver a win, he did exactly that, turning around an almost-lost position to beat Germany's Alexander Donchenko in Round 9 of the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.It was the kind of performance that felt like it could quiet the criticism all on its own.Playing black, Gukesh traded off his dark-squared bishop early to damage White's pawn structure, then spent the middlegame manoeuvring patiently, repositioning knights, expanding on the queenside with a5-a4, and probing for weaknesses without rushing.For a long stretch, the position stayed murky and roughly balanced, with both sides shuffling pieces and neither able to land a clean blow.It was in the run-up to the time control that things turned dangerous for Gukesh. Donchenko doubled his rooks on the e-file and pushed one all the way to e6, aiming squarely at Black's king, which had been forced to step out to f7 for safety.With his own clock running low, Gukesh had to defend precisely while trying to generate counterplay of his own on the kingside, pushing his h- and g-pawns forward to create complications.It was a position where one careless move could have ended the game in White's favour.Gukesh held his nerve. As the pawn storms and piece trades settled down, he found a route to activate his queen and knight while White's pieces drifted out of coordination.The Chennai-born grandmaster found an excellent move with 51...Nf4. The German sacked Gukesh's knight with 52.Rxf4, but Donchenko's bishop was thus left hanging on c3; Gukesh's queen swooped in to capture it, and from there it was a matter of technique.A check with his queen forced Donchenko's king into an impossible spot, and White resigned rather than play on a piece down with his king exposed.Elsewhere on the board, Nihal Sarin, playing white, spent much of his game in some turmoil against Frederik Svane but held firm for a draw.With Gukesh's win already banked, Praggnanandhaa and Arjun Erigaisi didn't need to force matters either, settling for draws against Vincent Keymer and Matthias Bluebaum, respectively. India closed out the match 2.5-1.5.With the win, India moved to 15 points, still one point behind hosts Uzbekistan, who beat the United States on Friday to stay in front.India's women's team also had a productive Friday, with Vantika Agrawal and Divya Deshmukh both delivering important wins to seal the match against Uzbekistan.Vantika, playing white against Nilufarkhon Imomkuzieva, picked up an early pawn with a sharp tactical sequence; a check with her queen forced Black's king to give up material before the middlegame had properly begun.She nursed that small material edge through a long, technical battle, trading down into a rook endgame where her extra pawn and more active king proved decisive.Pushing her kingside pawns forward in the closing stages, Vantika eventually broke through, and Imomkuzieva had no way to hold the position together.Divya Deshmukh's game against Gulrukhbegim Tokhirjonova was a far longer and more chaotic affair.Both sides grabbed material early. Tokhirjonova's knight snatched a pawn on b7 just as Divya's queen picked up a stray piece on d2, leaving the position roughly balanced but sharp.What followed was a marathon battle through the middlegame and into a complex rook, knight and bishop endgame, with both players navigating tricky technical positions deep into the game.Divya's technique held up better over the long haul, and after 73 hard-fought moves, Tokhirjonova had nothing left to stop Black's advancing king, resigning the position.Those two results were enough to see India through the match, keeping the team firmly in the mix for a medal.As things stand, India's women sit second in the standings on 15 points, behind an in-form Chinese side on 17.With two rounds left, India's hopes of gold now depend largely on whether China slip up, but on Friday's evidence, neither Indian team looks inclined to make things easy for anyone chasing them either.In the Open section, India face Uzbekistan 2, while the women’s team take on China in the penultimate round of the Chess Olympiad.
Article Summary: Dommaraju Gukesh turns around an almost-lost position to beat Germany's Alexander Donchenko in Round 9 of the 46th Chess Olympiad. India's women's team also had a productive Friday, with Vantika Agrawal and Divya Deshmukh both delivering important wins to seal the match.

Article Title: Gurgaon road rage: 4 men smash car window, then attack complainants outside police station
Article Text:
Four men allegedly got out of the SUV and tried to open his car door.





GURGAON: Four men allegedly intercepted a car and smashed its window on Thursday before attacking the complainant and two of his associates outside New Colony police station, where they had gone to lodge a complaint about the incident.The complainant, Gautam, a resident of Madanpuri, told police he was driving towards New Colony after taking a U-turn near Hari’s Bakery when a Scorpio N (HR26FG5726) overtook his car and forced him to stop.Four men allegedly got out of the SUV and tried to open his car door. When they failed, they allegedly smashed the window, and the broken glass hit Gautam’s face. He told police he suspected the men had come to rob him and were carrying illegal weapons.Gautam said he managed to drive away and called his friends Ravindra Kataria and Sandeep Dahiya. The three then went to New Colony police station to lodge a complaint. Gautam told police that a dashcam in his car had recorded the incident.Police said an emergency response vehicle received information about the incident near Aryan Hospital in Sector 7. A team reached the spot and found Gautam, Ravindra and Sandeep there, but the Scorpio had left.Police later found the SUV parked near Sai Temple at New Colony turn. Gautam told police its occupants had entered a hotel opposite the spot. A police team went to the hotel and found three men — Ajay , Mohit and Piyush Bhardwaj — in room 105. Police said the three had consumed alcohol and took them into custody.A fourth man, identified as Shivam, was apprehended while allegedly fighting with Gautam and his friends near the police station.Police said that after getting out of the police vehicle, Mohit joined Shivam and allegedly attacked Gautam, Ravindra and Sandeep near the station gate. Police personnel intervened and all four accused were taken for medical examination at Sector 10 govt hospital.Ravindra and Sandeep were also medically examined. Their reports recorded five and two injuries, respectively. Gautam also alleged that Ravindra’s gold chain went missing during the assault and that the accused threatened to kill them if they encountered them elsewhere.An FIR was registered at New Colony police station under sections 115(2), 126(2), 324(4), 351(3), 3(5) and 72(C) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Article Summary: Four men allegedly intercepted a car and smashed its window on Thursday. They then allegedly attacked the complainant and two of his associates outside New Colony police station, where they had gone to lodge a complaint about the incident. The complainant, Gautam, a resident of Madanpuri, told police he suspected the men had come to rob him.

Article Title: Last-minute dash, accomodation chaos, weight cut attempt: How Varun Sanyal's Asian Games nightmare unfolded
Article Text:

A fighter who almost wasn't there

The Games before the Games
